elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience (Agreement and/or Order Form)
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term."
Inserted clause uses "30 days' prior written notice", which is the preferred, not the 60–90 day fallback figure

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed; instead "Vendor shall provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a committed term" — no end-of-term/90-day Vendor right granted

reasons: All four atomic preferred elements are present in one concise inserted Section 9.4: Customer convenience right, 30 days' written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and express denial of any Vendor convenience right during a committed term.

The document had no convenience-termination clause, so a short insertion is the minimal fix; no other paragraph was rewritten and no new exception, undefined term or dangling mechanic was added ("Fees" and "Order Form" are defined).

Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (notice is 30 rather than 60–90 days, no early-termination fee mechanic, no end-of-term Vendor right), but that is irrelevant because the locked target level is preferred and preferred is fully met; the two levels are not combined.

Actionable refinement only: Section 2.1's take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" sits in tension with the new 9.4 — consider opening 9.4 with "Notwithstanding Section 2.1," so the exit right cannot be read as overridden by the purchase commitment.
